title: Daily Life - Going On A Diet
audio: mp3/187. Daily Life - Going On A Diet.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: Katherine – My name is Katherine and today we have an intermediate level lesson for you English learners out there.
segments.zh: 凯瑟琳——我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为你们的英语学习者准备了一个中级课程。

segments.en: Marco – That's right.
segments.zh: 马可——没错。

segments.en: On this occasion, we are going on a diet.
segments.zh: 在这个场合，我们要节食。

segments.en: So we're trying to lose weight.
segments.zh: 所以我们正在努力减肥。

segments.en: Katherine – Uh-oh.
segments.zh: 凯瑟琳——呃-哦。

segments.en: Well, there's a reason behind it.
segments.zh: 嗯，这背后是有原因的。

segments.en: Let's take a look at that reason in today's vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 让我们在今天的词汇预览中看看这个原因。

segments.en: Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预习。

segments.en: Marco – All right.
segments.zh: 马可——好吧。

segments.en: So today on Vocabulary Preview, we have a noun and it's a bridesmaid.
segments.zh: 所以今天在词汇预览中，我们有一个名词，它是伴娘。

segments.en: Katherine – A bridesmaid, a person.
segments.zh: 凯瑟琳——伴娘，一个人。

segments.en: So this is kind of like a job but it's a short job.
segments.zh: 所以这有点像一份工作，但它是一份短期的工作。

segments.en: You do it when your friend gets married.
segments.zh: 当你的朋友结婚时，你会这样做。

segments.en: It's the person, the woman who stands next to her friend on the friend's wedding day.
segments.zh: 是那个人，在朋友的婚礼上站在朋友旁边的女人。

segments.en: Marco – That's right.
segments.zh: 马可——没错。

segments.en: And usually bridesmaids want to lose weight because they have to get into this dress, right?
segments.zh: 通常伴娘想要减肥，因为他们必须穿上这件衣服，对吧？

segments.en: Katherine – That's right.
segments.zh: 凯瑟琳——没错。

segments.en: They have special dresses.
segments.zh: 他们有特殊的衣服。

segments.en: They have to make their friend look good.
segments.zh: 他们必须让他们的朋友看起来不错。

segments.en: They have to match each other actually because usually there's three or four girls.
segments.zh: 他们实际上必须相互匹配，因为通常有三四个女孩。

segments.en: They all have to wear the same outfit.
segments.zh: 他们都必须穿同样的衣服。

segments.en: So it's very stressful.
segments.zh: 所以压力很大。

segments.en: Marco – Okay.
segments.zh: 马可——好的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we're going to see what's going on in this dialogue and we'll be back shortly.
segments.zh: 所以我们将在这次对话中看到发生了什么，我们很快就会回来。

segments.en: Oh man, I've been starving myself for days now and I haven't lost an ounce.
segments.zh: 天哪，我都饿自己好几天了，体重却一丁点都没减。

segments.en: Are you trying to lose weight?
segments.zh: 你想减肥吗？

segments.en: Yeah, my friend is getting married next month and I'm supposed to be a bridesmaid.
segments.zh: 是的，我的朋友下个月要结婚了，我应该做伴娘。

segments.en: I have to fit into my dress and look nice for her wedding, but I haven't lost any weight.
segments.zh: 我得穿得下那条裙子，在她婚礼上漂漂亮亮的，可体重一点也没降。

segments.en: Look at these love handles.
segments.zh: 看看我腰两边的赘肉。

segments.en: You don't have to starve yourself to lose weight.
segments.zh: 减肥不需要饿着自己。

segments.en: I think that's where you're going wrong.
segments.zh: 我认为这就是你出错的地方。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: If I eat less, then my body will start eating away at my fat reserves, right?
segments.zh: 如果我吃得少，那么我的身体就会开始吃掉我的脂肪储备，对吧？

segments.en: Not really.
segments.zh: 也不是。

segments.en: You should try to not eat foods high in calories, salts or saturated fats.
segments.zh: 你应该尽量不要吃富含卡路里、盐或饱和脂肪的食物。

segments.en: Stay away from oily food and artificial flavors.
segments.zh: 远离油腻的食物和人造香料。

segments.en: So you're saying that I should eat, but I should just watch what I eat?
segments.zh: 所以你是说，我还是应该吃，只是要注意吃些什么？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: You should also try to reduce your intake of carbohydrates and foods that are high in cholesterol.
segments.zh: 您还应该尝试减少碳水化合物和高胆固醇食物的摄入量。

segments.en: You can have steamed veggies or increase your protein intake found in chicken or fish.
segments.zh: 您可以吃蒸蔬菜或增加鸡肉或鱼中的蛋白质摄入量。

segments.en: If I do all of this, you think I can lose 20 pounds in four weeks?
segments.zh: 如果我做这一切，你认为我可以在四个星期内减掉 20 磅吗？

segments.en: Don't count on it.
segments.zh: 别指望了。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We're back.
segments.zh: 我们回来了。

segments.en: So I think there were a lot of interesting words related to food and to losing weight.
segments.zh: 所以我认为有很多与食物和减肥有关的有趣词。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look now at language takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不现在看看语言外卖。

segments.en: Language takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay, this first phrase in language takeaway is a phrase that the girl says about herself.
segments.zh: 好吧，语言外卖中的第一个短语是女孩所说的关于她自己的短语。

segments.en: She's trying to lose weight.
segments.zh: 她正在努力减肥。

segments.en: She's been starving herself or she says, I've been starving myself.
segments.zh: 她一直在挨饿，或者她说，我一直在挨饿。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I've been starving myself.
segments.zh: 我一直在饿死自己。

segments.en: So to starve yourself is to make yourself not eat.
segments.zh: 所以饿死自己就是让自己不吃。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So to starve is a verb.
segments.zh: 所以饿死是一个动词。

segments.en: It means to not give someone food.
segments.zh: 这意味着不给别人食物。

segments.en: But to starve yourself, to starve oneself is reflexive.
segments.zh: 但饿死自己，饿死自己是反思的。

segments.en: I'm doing it to myself and it means that I'm not giving myself any food.
segments.zh: 我对自己这样做，这意味着我没有给自己任何食物。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you're starving yourself basically to lose weight.
segments.zh: 所以你基本上是为了减肥而饿死自己。

segments.en: And she said, well, I've been starving myself for days and I haven't lost an ounce.
segments.zh: 她说，好吧，我已经饿了好几天了，我还没有损失一盎司。

segments.en: What is an ounce?
segments.zh: 什么是盎司？

segments.en: It's a good question.
segments.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

segments.en: An ounce is a kind of weight.
segments.zh: 一盎司是一种重量。

segments.en: So like a kilogram or a gram or a pound, but an ounce is a very, very small measurement.
segments.zh: 所以就像一公斤或一克或一磅，但一盎司是一个非常非常小的尺寸。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And this is in the imperial system.
segments.zh: 这是在帝国体系中。

segments.en: So maybe a lot of our listeners aren't familiar with it, but usually for example, pounds and ounces go together just like grams and kilograms.
segments.zh: 所以也许我们的很多听众都不熟悉它，但通常，磅和盎司就像克和公斤一样。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So I might be wrong.
segments.zh: 所以我可能错了。

segments.en: I think there are 16 ounces in a pound.
segments.zh: 我想一磅有 16 盎司。

segments.en: So if you think about it, a pound, you say, oh, I lost a pound.
segments.zh: 所以如果你想一想，一磅，你说，哦，我减了一磅。

segments.en: 16 ounces.
segments.zh: 16盎司。

segments.en: She hasn't even lost an ounce.
segments.zh: 她甚至没有损失一盎司。

segments.en: It's a way to say she hasn't lost any weight yet.
segments.zh: 这是一种说她还没有减肥的方式。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So she was complaining about not losing weight and she said, look at these love handles.
segments.zh: 所以她在抱怨没有减肥，她说，看看这些爱情把手。

segments.en: What are love handles?
segments.zh: 什么是爱情手柄？

segments.en: I love this phrase because you can like imagine them.
segments.zh: 我喜欢这句话，因为你可以想象它们。

segments.en: So imagine hugging someone and your hands are on their waist and maybe they have a little extra fat.
segments.zh: 所以想象一下拥抱某人，你的手放在他们的腰间，也许他们有一点额外的脂肪。

segments.en: Those are like love handles.
segments.zh: 那些就像爱情把手。

segments.en: You know, a handle is what you have on a door.
segments.zh: 你知道，把手是你在门上的东西。

segments.en: You turn the handle and the door opens.
segments.zh: 你转动把手，门打开。

segments.en: But these are, this is fat on someone's side.
segments.zh: 但这些是，这对某人来说是脂肪。

segments.en: So a man or a woman can have fat on their hips and this is called love handles.
segments.zh: 所以男人或女人的臀部可能有脂肪，这被称为爱情把手。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So love handles.
segments.zh: 所以爱情把手。

segments.en: It's a nice way of saying that extra little fat that people have on their sides.
segments.zh: 这是一种很好的方式来表达人们两边的额外小脂肪。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And now talking more specifically about words related to food, we have one that maybe most of you are familiar with, calories.
segments.zh: 现在更具体地谈论与食物有关的词，我们可能有很多人熟悉的卡路里。

segments.en: Calories.
segments.zh: 卡路里。

segments.en: So calorie is a measurement of energy in food.
segments.zh: 所以卡路里是食物中能量的量度。

segments.en: And so a lot of women and some men too like to avoid eating many calories.
segments.zh: 所以很多女人和一些男人也喜欢避免摄入很多卡路里。

segments.en: They say, oh, that Snickers bar that has 1000 calories.
segments.zh: 他们说，哦，那个有 1000 卡路里的士力架酒吧。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: If actually, if you look at your food labels, it usually says that you should have a daily diet should include more or less 2000 calories.
segments.zh: 如果实际上，如果您查看您的食品标签，它通常会说您应该每天饮食中包含或多或少的 2000 卡路里。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Another thing to avoid are saturated fats.
segments.zh: 要避免的另一件事是饱和脂肪。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So there's fat and there's saturated fat.
segments.zh: 所以有脂肪，也有饱和脂肪。

segments.en: Marco, what's the difference?
segments.zh: 马可，有什么区别？

segments.en: I have no idea.
segments.zh: 我完全不知道。

segments.en: Come on.
segments.zh: 来吧。

segments.en: There are two different types of fats.
segments.zh: 有两种不同类型的脂肪。

segments.en: Some of them are good for you.
segments.zh: 其中一些对你有好处。

segments.en: Your body needs fat, right?
segments.zh: 你的身体需要脂肪，对吧？

segments.en: But saturated fats are the ones that are more difficult for your body to absorb and to make them work for you.
segments.zh: 但是饱和脂肪是你的身体更难吸收和让它们为你工作的脂肪。

segments.en: So usually they accumulate and that's why maybe they will, for example, make you a little bit fatter.
segments.zh: 所以通常它们会积累，这就是为什么它们可能会让你变胖一些。

segments.en: So a lot of sweets have saturated fats.
segments.zh: 所以很多糖果都有饱和脂肪。

segments.en: Oily foods have saturated fats and it's good to avoid those.
segments.zh: 油性食物含有饱和脂肪，避免这些食物是好的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So stay away from saturated fats and artificial flavors.
segments.zh: 所以远离饱和脂肪和人造香料。

segments.en: So the word artificial can be used with many different things.
segments.zh: 所以人工这个词可以与许多不同的东西一起使用。

segments.en: It means fake, not natural.
segments.zh: 这意味着假的，不是自然的。

segments.en: So you could say you have artificial flowers or artificial scents.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说你有人造花或人造气味。

segments.en: But in this case, we have artificial flavors.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，我们有人造香料。

segments.en: That means fake flavors.
segments.zh: 这意味着假口味。

segments.en: It's orange flavored, but there's no oranges.
segments.zh: 它是橙味的，但没有橙子。

segments.en: It never came from an orange.
segments.zh: 它从来没有来自橙色。

segments.en: You have to be careful with these because they use, because in many food products, chemicals are used.
segments.zh: 你必须小心这些，因为它们使用，因为在许多食品中，使用了化学品。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And sugars, for example.
segments.zh: 和糖，例如。

segments.en: So as you said, if you want to make something taste like orange, maybe they will use different chemicals and sugars to make it taste like orange.
segments.zh: 所以正如你所说，如果你想做一些像橙子一样的东西，也许他们会使用不同的化学物质和糖来让它尝起来像橙子。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: The last thing we have to avoid is this word cholesterol.
segments.zh: 我们要避免的最后一件事是这个词胆固醇。

segments.en: Cholesterol.
segments.zh: 胆固醇。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So these are found, for example, in eggs have a lot of cholesterol.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，在鸡蛋中发现了这些胆固醇。

segments.en: Or even just meats in general, like red meat.
segments.zh: 甚至只是一般的肉类，比如红肉。

segments.en: And so people with heart problems are told to avoid cholesterol because it can actually, it can prevent the blood going to your heart.
segments.zh: 因此，患有心脏病的人被告知要避免胆固醇，因为它实际上可以防止血液流向您的心脏。

segments.en: It blocks up your heart.
segments.zh: 它阻塞了你的心。

segments.en: So cholesterol is another bad one.
segments.zh: 所以胆固醇是另一种糟糕的胆固醇。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So all of these words are nouns and they're related to dieting and to food.
segments.zh: 所以所有这些词都是名词，它们与节食和食物有关。

segments.en: So I think we should listen to this dialogue again and keep a lookout for these words.
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们应该再次听这个对话，并留意这些话。

segments.en: Oh man, I've been starving myself for days now and I haven't lost an ounce.
segments.zh: 天哪，我都饿自己好几天了，体重却一丁点都没减。

segments.en: Are you trying to lose weight?
segments.zh: 你想减肥吗？

segments.en: Yeah, my friend is getting married next month and I'm supposed to be a bridesmaid.
segments.zh: 是的，我的朋友下个月要结婚了，我应该做伴娘。

segments.en: I have to fit into my dress and look nice for her wedding, but I haven't lost any weight.
segments.zh: 我得穿得下那条裙子，在她婚礼上漂漂亮亮的，可体重一点也没降。

segments.en: Look at these love handles.
segments.zh: 看看这些爱情手柄。

segments.en: You don't have to starve yourself to lose weight.
segments.zh: 减肥不需要饿着自己。

segments.en: I think that's where you're going wrong.
segments.zh: 我认为这就是你出错的地方。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: If I eat less than my body will start eating away at my fat reserves, right?
segments.zh: 如果我吃的少于我的身体会开始消耗我的脂肪储备，对吧？

segments.en: Not really.
segments.zh: 也不是。

segments.en: You should try to not eat foods high in calories, salts or saturated fats.
segments.zh: 你应该尽量不要吃富含卡路里、盐或饱和脂肪的食物。

segments.en: Stay away from oily food and artificial flavors.
segments.zh: 远离油腻的食物和人造香料。

segments.en: So you're saying that I should eat, but I should just watch what I eat?
segments.zh: 所以你是说，我还是应该吃，只是要注意吃些什么？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: You can also try to reduce your intake of carbohydrates and foods that are high in cholesterol.
segments.zh: 您还可以尝试减少碳水化合物和高胆固醇食物的摄入量。

segments.en: You can have steamed veggies or increase your protein intake found in chicken or fish.
segments.zh: 您可以吃蒸蔬菜或增加鸡肉或鱼中的蛋白质摄入量。

segments.en: If I do all of this, you think I can lose 20 pounds in four weeks?
segments.zh: 如果我做这一切，你认为我可以在四个星期内减掉 20 磅吗？

segments.en: Don't count on it.
segments.zh: 别指望了。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: We're going to take a look at two phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 我们将在 Fluency Builder 上看看两个短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay, this first phrase is something that the girl who is dieting says.
segments.zh: 好吧，第一个短语是节食的女孩说的。

segments.en: She says, are you saying that I should eat?
segments.zh: 她说，你是说我应该吃饭吗？

segments.en: Because she's starving herself.
segments.zh: 因为她自己饿死了。

segments.en: But that the important thing is that I watch what I eat.
segments.zh: 但重要的是我看我吃的东西。

segments.en: So what is this watch what I eat?
segments.zh: 那么我吃什么的手表是什么？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So to watch what you eat is to be careful of what you eat or to take care.
segments.zh: 所以看你吃什么就是小心你吃的东西或照顾。

segments.en: So it doesn't actually mean to look at your food a lot.
segments.zh: 所以这实际上并不意味着经常看你的食物。

segments.en: You don't have to stare at your food.
segments.zh: 你不必盯着你的食物。

segments.en: You just have to be careful or to pay attention to what you're eating.
segments.zh: 你只需要小心或注意你吃的东西。

segments.en: So you should watch what you eat.
segments.zh: 所以你应该注意你吃的东西。

segments.en: So that means pay attention.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着要注意。

segments.en: Does it have lots of calories?
segments.zh: 它有很多卡路里吗？

segments.en: Is there a lot of cholesterol?
segments.zh: 有很多胆固醇吗？

segments.en: Things like this.
segments.zh: 像这样的事情。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: For example, you may see signs in some places that say, watch your step.
segments.zh: 例如，您可能会在某些地方看到“注意您的步伐”的迹象。

segments.en: So be careful where you're stepping.
segments.zh: 所以要小心你走的地方。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, this next phrase is the very last phrase.
segments.zh: 好吧，下一个短语是最后一个短语。

segments.en: The friend says, do you think I can lose 20 pounds?
segments.zh: 朋友说，你觉得我能减掉20磅吗？

segments.en: And for those of you who use kilos, this is about eight kilos.
segments.zh: 对于那些使用公斤的人来说，这大约是八公斤。

segments.en: That's a lot of weight.
segments.zh: 那是很大的重量。

segments.en: And the answer is don't count on it.
segments.zh: 答案是不要指望它。

segments.en: So what is this don't count on it?
segments.zh: 那么这是什么不指望它呢？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Don't count on it.
segments.zh: 别指望了。

segments.en: Take that as a phrase.
segments.zh: 把它当作一个短语。

segments.en: It basically means that probably won't happen.
segments.zh: 这基本上意味着这可能不会发生。

segments.en: So you think you can come to my birthday party?
segments.zh: 所以你认为你可以来参加我的生日聚会吗？

segments.en: No, don't count on it.
segments.zh: 不，不要指望它。

segments.en: I'll be busy.
segments.zh: 我会很忙。

segments.en: Oh, so that means that means he probably won't.
segments.zh: 哦，这意味着他可能不会。

segments.en: Marco probably won't come.
segments.zh: 马可可能不会来。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you shouldn't expect it to happen because he can't promise that it will.
segments.zh: 所以你不应该期望它会发生，因为他不能保证它会发生。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's a good way of putting it.
segments.zh: 这是一个很好的表达方式。

segments.en: Don't expect it to happen.
segments.zh: 不要指望它会发生。

segments.en: So for example, don't count on winning the lottery anytime soon.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，不要指望很快中彩票。

segments.en: Why not?
segments.zh: 为什么不呢？

segments.en: Because it's very difficult, right?
segments.zh: 因为这很困难，对吧？

segments.en: So don't count on it.
segments.zh: 所以不要指望它。

segments.en: Or you can say, don't count on this train being on time.
segments.zh: 或者你可以说，不要指望这列火车准时。

segments.en: It's always at least a half an hour late.
segments.zh: 它总是迟到至少半个小时。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So many different examples there.
segments.zh: 那里有很多不同的例子。

segments.en: I think we should listen to a dialogue for the last time.
segments.zh: 我认为我们应该最后一次听对话。

segments.en: Oh man, I've been starving myself for days now and I haven't lost an ounce.
segments.zh: 天哪，我都饿自己好几天了，体重却一丁点都没减。

segments.en: Are you trying to lose weight?
segments.zh: 你想减肥吗？

segments.en: Yeah, my friend is getting married next month and I'm supposed to be a bridesmaid.
segments.zh: 是的，我的朋友下个月要结婚了，我应该做伴娘。

segments.en: I have to fit into my dress and look nice for her wedding, but I haven't lost any weight.
segments.zh: 我得穿得下那条裙子，在她婚礼上漂漂亮亮的，可体重一点也没降。

segments.en: Look at these love handles.
segments.zh: 看看这些爱情手柄。

segments.en: You don't have to starve yourself to lose weight.
segments.zh: 减肥不需要饿着自己。

segments.en: I think that's where you're going wrong.
segments.zh: 我认为这就是你出错的地方。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: If I eat less, then my body will start eating away at my fat reserves, right?
segments.zh: 如果我吃得少，那么我的身体就会开始吃掉我的脂肪储备，对吧？

segments.en: Not really.
segments.zh: 也不是。

segments.en: You should try to not eat foods high in calories, salts, or saturated fats.
segments.zh: 你应该尽量不要吃富含卡路里、盐分或饱和脂肪的食物。

segments.en: Stay away from oily food and artificial flavors.
segments.zh: 远离油腻的食物和人造香料。

segments.en: So you're saying that I should eat, but I should just watch what I eat?
segments.zh: 所以你是说，我还是应该吃，只是要注意吃些什么？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: You can also try to reduce your intake of carbohydrates and foods that are high in cholesterol.
segments.zh: 您还可以尝试减少碳水化合物和高胆固醇食物的摄入量。

segments.en: You can have steamed veggies or increase your protein intake found in chicken or fish.
segments.zh: 您可以吃蒸蔬菜或增加鸡肉或鱼中的蛋白质摄入量。

segments.en: If I do all of this, you think I can lose 20 pounds in four weeks?
segments.zh: 如果我做这一切，你认为我可以在四个星期内减掉 20 磅吗？

segments.en: Don't count on it.
segments.zh: 别指望了。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So these are some pretty healthy tips, right?
segments.zh: 所以这些是一些非常健康的技巧，对吧？

segments.en: Watch what you eat and don't starve yourself.
segments.zh: 注意你吃什么，不要饿死自己。

segments.en: Absolutely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: Starving yourself, I think is, well, obviously very unhealthy.
segments.zh: 饿死自己，我认为，嗯，显然非常不健康。

segments.en: To starve, to die of starvation, that's the noun.
segments.zh: 饿死，饿死，这就是名词。

segments.en: Not a very pretty way to go.
segments.zh: 不是一个非常漂亮的方法。

segments.en: I've actually also heard that people that start to eat less, right?
segments.zh: 其实我也听说过少吃的人，对吧？

segments.en: To maybe just eat once a day, their body actually thinks that there isn't much food around, so they start to store up these fats and these calories, energy, instead of releasing them normally.
segments.zh: 也许每天只吃一次，他们的身体实际上认为周围没有太多的食物，所以他们开始储存这些脂肪和这些卡路里、能量，而不是正常释放它们。

segments.en: So instead of actually losing weight, you actually gain weight because the moment that you eat, your body stores everything.
segments.zh: 因此，您实际上并没有减肥，而是因为吃东西的那一刻，您的身体会储存一切。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So instead of getting rid of those good fats, your body stores them with the saturated fats and you are doing the opposite to your body that you should be doing.
segments.zh: 因此，与其摆脱那些好脂肪，不如将它们与饱和脂肪一起储存，而你的身体与你的身体相反，你应该做的事情。

segments.en: So the best recommendation that I've always heard is to avoid eating too much red meat, balance your diet out, eat lots of fruit as well, have those good sugars, and avoid artificial foods.
segments.zh: 所以我一直听到的最好的建议是避免吃太多的红肉，平衡饮食，吃大量的水果，吃那些好的糖，避免人工食品。

segments.en: Drink a lot of water.
segments.zh: 多喝水。

segments.en: Drink a lot of water and exercise.
segments.zh: 多喝水和运动。

segments.en: Exercise, yeah.
segments.zh: 锻炼，是的。

segments.en: This is the key thing.
segments.zh: 这是关键的事情。

segments.en: I think many people rely only on dieting or eating less, but actually nothing can take its place more than exercise.
segments.zh: 我认为许多人只依赖节食或少吃，但实际上没有什么比运动更能取代它的位置。

segments.en: And exercise is really great because it tones those muscles, so once you actually lose the weight, you feel good, you have muscles, you have more energy, and it helps you sleep.
segments.zh: 运动真的很棒，因为它可以调理这些肌肉，所以一旦你真正减轻了体重，你就会感觉良好，你有肌肉，你有更多的能量，它可以帮助你入睡。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So some sound advice here at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 所以在 Englishpod 上有一些合理的建议。

segments.en: And if you have any other questions or doubts, visit our website, EnglishPod.com, and we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何其他问题或疑问，请访问我们的网站 Englishpod.com，我们将在那里见到大家。

segments.en: Happy studies and until next time.
segments.zh: 快乐的学习，直到下一次。

segments.en: Bye, everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。
